name: Office of Financial Research (U.S. Treasury) — Financial Stress Index
description: The Office of Financial Research, a bureau of the U.S. Treasury Department created by the Dodd-Frank Act. Its public-facing OFR Financial Stress Index (FSI) is a daily market-based snapshot of stress in global financial markets, built from 33 financial market variables (yield spreads, valuation measures, interest rates) split into five stress categories and three regions.

notes: One CSV holds the national FSI plus all eight sub-indexes as columns: Date, OFR FSI, Credit, Equity valuation, Safe assets, Funding, Volatility, United States, Other advanced economies, Emerging markets.
Checked 2026-09-15: 6,757 daily rows from 2000-01-03 through 2026-09-11 (today minus 2 business days), 200 OK, content-type text/csv, no auth or key required.

No API for the FSI itself: /financial-stress-index/api/ and /financial-stress-index/download/ both 404. The OFR does run separate APIs for its Short-Term Funding Monitor and Hedge Fund Monitor (financialresearch.gov/data/), unrelated products not otherwise researched here.
The FSI page states 'The FSI publishes with data that is current from two business days prior' and 'The index is calculated after each U.S. trading day.'

terms.summary: No explicit copyright or reuse/redistribution statement found for the FSI data itself. The FSI page carries only a suggested citation ('Office of Financial Research, "OFR Financial Stress Index," refreshed daily, https://www.financialresearch.gov/financial-stress-index/ (accessed ).') and a general liability disclaimer; a separate disclaimer on the same page about copyrighted material with reuse restrictions is explicitly scoped to non-OFR external sites the OFR links to, not to the FSI's own published values. As a U.S. Treasury bureau, OFR's own works are presumptively U.S. government works (17 U.S.C. 105), but no page states this.

datasets.name: OFR Financial Stress Index (national, category and region sub-indexes)
datasets.gives: The national OFR FSI, its five stress-category sub-indexes (credit, equity valuation, safe assets, funding, volatility), and its three region sub-indexes (United States, other advanced economies, emerging markets), all in one CSV keyed by date
notes: Positive reads above-average stress, negative below-average, per the FSI page's own description.

The 33 underlying market variables (rates, spreads, implied vol, etc.) are themselves drawn from a mix of sources (e.g. market data vendors, other agencies); the FSI page does not itemize their individual licences, and whether any restrict republication of the derived index values was not established here — see catalog/research-log.md.
'unit' inferred from the page's own description of the index as standard-deviation-style stress readings around zero, not stated verbatim as a unit label; treat as approximate.

notes: Short-Term Funding Monitor (data.financialresearch.gov API, five datasets: money market funds, repo markets, NY Fed reference rates, NY Fed primary dealer statistics, Treasury constant maturity rates) was checked but not catalogued as a dataset here — out of scope for this pass (only the FSI was assigned); its API auth/rate-limit/terms are unresearched.
Hedge Fund Monitor API (financialresearch.gov/hedge-fund-monitor/api/) exists but is unrelated to the FSI and was not researched.
